subject: zombie
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: zombie, in the place of the game's models/zombie.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/hgrunt.mdl, models/barney.mdl, models/islave.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 3 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, C, C where the asset was B, D, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Outline matches the brief's words in all ten views: about 68 units tall (measured 68.4), upright, with a forward stoop of head and shoulders in the left and right views. The long arms reach out to the sides and forward in the front and top views. The stoop is moderate rather than deep, but no part sticks out or is missing.

M2.reason: The brief gives height only, about 68. Measured height is 68.4 (0.6% off), and the length and width (38.5 and 53.8) are within the bounds of a standing figure with arms out.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, listed down to the small: parasite body over the head (yellow-tan bulb, front, side and top views); lab coat with sleeves, collar and torn chest opening (front, back and side views); the chest wound showing ribs and organs (front and back); trousers and bloodied shoes (all views); two long clawed hands, each with four fingers and a curved claw at each tip (front, back and top views, and the attack frames). Claws are present at the fingertips at game size. Nothing asked for is missing. The coat's tearing is mainly the chest opening, not the sleeves or hem, which stay whole.

M4.reason: The coat is white with red blood staining, the parasite head is fleshy yellow-tan, the arms and claws are dark red-brown, and the trousers are pale with blood marks. Each region matches its material in the brief (cloth, flesh, bloody shoes). No region has a wrong colour or material.

M5.reason: Blood smears on the coat and legs, a painted torn cavity with rib detail on the chest (front and back), and darker bloodied shoes are there and read at the size the game shows them. Nothing is smeared or noisy beyond the brief's bloodied look.

M6.reason: Scored 2 as the line-up measure sets it. In the line-up of four (asset at A beside three Half-Life models), the shuffled tests picked the other models as the one not made by Valve in each run, so the asset passed for one of the game's.

M7.reason: The front is the front: the chest opening, head and hands face the front view. The figure stands upright on both feet, which sit on the floor line in the walk and attack frames, and the origin is at the feet.

M8.reason: Triangles 844: under the bar of 1,008 (twice the median of 504, which is larger than the third quartile of 731) and well under Valve's most (1,640). The kit's warning at the third quartile is passed over and noted. Nothing visible is open or floating. The underside of the torso (below view) is dark inside, but a player never sees it, which is Valve's practice.

C1.reason: Walk frames (0 to 59) and attack frames (0 to 35) show every part on the body. Arms swing from the shoulders and the rear foot lifts properly in walk frame 51. In attack frames 10 to 25 the claw arm sweeps out and across the chest and stays attached. Nothing comes apart, sinks or floats. The frames are small, so the finest finger movement can't be checked at this scale.
